memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then Rachel and Leah replied, 'Do we still have any share in the inheritance of our father's estate? Does he not regard us as foreigners? Not only has he sold us, but he has used up what was paid for us. Surely all the wealth that God took away from our father belongs to us and our children. So do whatever God has told you.'" - Gen 31:14-16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Jacob's two wives — who had spent years in rivalry with each other — now speak with one voice. Rachel and Leah agree together: their father Laban had treated them poorly, even "sold" them and used up their bride-price. They see clearly that their future lies not with Laban but with Jacob and, above all, with God's leading. Their conclusion is simple and united: "So do whatever God has told you."

It is striking to see these sisters, so often divided, brought together by a shared trust in God's direction. When the will of God becomes the deciding factor, it has a way of uniting people who might otherwise pull in different directions. The question was no longer "what do I want?" but "what has God said?"

This is a good pattern for any family or partnership. So many conflicts arise when each person is chasing their own preference. But when a household agrees together, "Let us do whatever God has told us," unity follows. God's will becomes the common ground on which people can stand side by side.

Is there division in your home, your friendships, or your church? Often the path to unity is to stop asking "whose way will win?" and start asking together, "What is God calling us to do?" Shared obedience to God is a powerful bond.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I seek God's will together with those I share life with?
2. Where could shared obedience to God bring unity in a divided situation?
3. Am I asking "what do I want?" or "what has God said?"

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, unite my heart with others around Your will. Where there is division, help us to ask together not whose way will win, but what You are calling us to do. Amen.
